text:
Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorksInLibrary(x) ::: x currently works in the library.
FromCS(x) ::: x is from the computer science department.
HasPartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
TakesDatabaseCourse(x) ::: x is taking the database course.
TakesWithDavid(x) ::: x is taking a class with Professor David.
WorksInLab(x) ::: x is working in the lab.
Premises:
∀x (Student(x) ∧ WorksInLibrary(x) → ¬FromCS(x)) ::: None of the students who currently work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x (Student(x) ∧ HasPartTimeJob(x) → WorksInLibrary(x)) ::: All of the students with part-time jobs offered by the university currently work in the library.
∀x (TakesDatabaseCourse(x) → FromCS(x)) ::: All of the students who are taking the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (TakesWithDavid(x) → TakesDatabaseCourse(x)) ::: All of the students taking a class with Professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (WorksInLab(x) → TakesWithDavid(x)) ::: All students working in the lab are taking a class with Professor David.
WorksInLab(james) ::: James is a student working in the lab.
¬WorksInLab(james) ∨ ¬HasPartTimeJob(james) ::: James doesn't work in the lab or have a part-time job offered by the university.
Conclusion:
TakesDatabaseCourse(james) ::: James takes the database course.
